question: In a medical store, the marked price of an injection is ₹6,490. The medical store owner gives a discount of 18% on its sale. What is the sale price (in ₹) of the injection? (Rounded off to the nearest rupee.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price = Marked Price × Multiplying factor for discount

SP = 6490 × (100 − 18)%

SP = 6490 × 0.82

SP = 5321.8 ≈ 5322 (Rounded off to nearest rupee)

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,322.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of the injection = ₹6,490

Discount percentage = 18%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 
 MP
 ₹6490
 
 
 SP
 ₹5322
 
 
• 
 

 −18% Discount
 × 0.82

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 6490 × (100 − 18) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 6490 × 82 ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 649 × 8.2

⇒ SP = 5321.8

⇒ Rounding off to the nearest rupee, SP ≈ 5322

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,322.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. It represents the reduction in price offered by the seller. The direct formula is Discount = MP − SP.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of D₁% and D₂% are given, the Effective Discount Percentage is equivalent to: (D₁ + D₂ − (D₁ × D₂) ÷ 100)%.

Profit/Loss vs Discount Relation

Profit or Loss is always evaluated over the Cost Price (CP), whereas Discount applies to the Marked Price (MP). They are linked by the fundamental relation: CP × (100 + Profit%) = MP × (100 − Discount%).
